answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a costly, verifiable resource before it may transact — for example a deposit locked in escrow that only a real, reputation-bearing participant can afford to lose. Picture timber cut from one small island forest: every plank is scarce, so a single actor cannot cheaply build a thousand fake houses. Like an ocean that dilutes one drop, a network that prices each identity with real cost makes mass forgery unprofitable while honest agents keep trading freely.
